reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses strengthening mechanisms in BCC HEAs and microstructural inversion for ductility, but neither provides specific support for Mo-induced precipitation in TiVNbTa, its effect on high-temperature strength, or its impact on thermal conductivity. The key premises lack direct prior evidence.
premises: Mo addition to TiVNbTa will form finely dispersed Mo-rich precipitates in the BCC matrix
These precipitates will enhance high-temperature yield strength and creep resistance via dispersion/precipitation strengthening
The modified alloy will retain room-temperature ductility
The modified alloy will maintain efficient thermal conductivity for the W-to-CuCrZr interface
